appraisal_events.evidence: « Comment ça, à l'Élysée ? » cria le docteur Cottard d'une voix tonnante. – Oui, chez M. Grévy, répondit Swann, un peu gêné de l'effet que sa phrase avait produit.
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann's offhand mention of lunching with the Préfet de police at the Élysée (M. Grévy's residence) registers in the Verdurin circle as an unexpected sign of access to the highest official world, drawing Cottard's astonished reaction, though Swann himself is visibly uncomfortable at having revealed it.

status_effects.explanation: The casual reveal of a lunch at the Élysée marks Swann, within this bourgeois salon, as connected to the summit of official society, a brief elevation he himself seems to shy away from.

ambiguities: Cottard's loud outburst ('cria... d'une voix tonnante') can be read primarily as evidence of his own excitability (as the accepted annotation captures) and/or as a register of astonishment at Swann's grand connections; both readings are compatible and the supplement event does not contradict the accepted diminishment of Cottard.

Le peintre's joke at Cottard's expense is treated as part of the already-captured movement diminishing Cottard, since the passage gives le peintre no distinct outcome of his own, so he was not separately scored.
M. Grévy appears only as the named location/host of the lunch ('chez M. Grévy') with no evaluative content attached to him, so he was not scored.
